steps.description: Fit the differential expression model on the delivered log2(TPM + 1) matrix. (1) Value-range check first: confirm the matrix is log-scale (approximately 0-20, fractional values) and not an integer count table; if it looks like counts, stop and report that rather than proceeding. (2) No normalization — the values already carry the facility's normalization, and a second normalization would hide it. (3) Filter low-expression genes on mean log expression, using a floor read from the low end of the distribution, or requiring a gene to exceed the floor in at least as many samples as the smallest group (6); the floor must be chosen without reference to the condition labels so the filter stays independent of the test. Report the number of genes kept. (4) Build design ~0 + condition with the condition factor levels set explicitly, control as reference, and a named contrast treated - control so a positive log2 fold change means higher in treated. (5) lmFit then eBayes with trend=TRUE and robust=TRUE. (6) topTable with adjust.method="BH", number=Inf; call DE genes by adjusted p-value < 0.05. If a minimum effect size is wanted, obtain it with treat()/topTreat() against that log2 fold-change threshold inside the model — never by filtering the estimated logFC after a zero-null test. Output a full results table (gene, logFC, AveExpr, t, P.Value, adj.P.Val, B) for every tested gene, the significant subset, a volcano plot, and an MA-style plot.

plan.title: Treated vs control muscle DE on log2 expression
plan.analytical_narrative:
The core facility delivered a 12000 x 12 matrix of log2(TPM + 1) values (/data/inputs/expression/log_expr.csv) with a 12-row sample table (/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv): 6 treated vs 6 control human muscle samples, unpaired, single batch. No counts exist, so the negative-binomial route (DESeq2, edgeR, limma-voom) is not available and must not be faked by rounding or back-transforming values into pseudo-counts. The plan therefore runs the limma linear model directly on the delivered log-scale values with an empirical Bayes step that uses the mean-variance trend and robust hyperparameter estimation.

T1S1 establishes sample structure before any model: PCA/MDS on the 500 most variable genes, a sample-distance heatmap, and per-sample value distributions, coloured by condition. This is where an outlier or an unlabelled processing split would surface; with n=6 per group a single aberrant sample can drive the whole contrast, so the QC verdict is stated explicitly rather than assumed.

T1S2 does the test. It first confirms the values really are log2-scale (roughly 0-20, fractional, not large integers) — the profile says log2(TPM + 1), and this check is what protects against a mislabelled count table. It does not renormalize. It filters on mean log expression with a floor set independently of the condition labels, fits ~0 + condition with an explicit treated-vs-control contrast, and calls eBayes(trend=TRUE, robust=TRUE). Significance is taken from BH-adjusted p-values, and any biologically motivated fold-change threshold is tested inside the model via treat() rather than applied post hoc to the estimates.

T1S3 writes the report: method and package versions, the design and the contrast direction, the thresholds, the number of genes tested after filtering, the number of DE genes, and sessionInfo. The research question asks only which genes differ, so no enrichment step is planned — that would be unasked scope. Honest limits to carry through: 12 samples give modest power, TPM-derived values carry the facility's own normalization choices which cannot be audited from here, and the absence of counts means no count-based dispersion modelling and no independent replication of the facility's pipeline.

limma-trend linear model with robust eBayes
topTable BH adjustment
